title: 5.15.2 Sub-build: Am I in my own tail?
description: A body that follows you will eventually meet you. Ask the question every step, before you move.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: The snake crosses its own body and nothing happens. The lose rule is missing.

steps.title: Ask the question
steps.instructions: Before moving, loop over the body and compare each segment with the cell the head is about to enter: `if (seg.x === nextX && seg.y === nextY) { ... }`.
hints: Compare cells with `===`, not overlaps: both are integers on the grid.
Check the target cell, not where the head is now.

steps.title: Set the flag
steps.instructions: Inside that `if`, set a `lost` flag and stop stepping. In `draw()`, show "Game over" when `lost` is true.
hints: Do not delete the snake: the round ends, the game stays on screen.

requirements.title: A loop over the body
requirements.description: Every segment is tested against the head's next cell. Help: 5.15.1 (Reading: Searching the array)
requirements.hint: for (const seg of body) { if (seg.x === nextX && seg.y === nextY) ... }

requirements.title: The round ends
requirements.description: A lost/over flag is set when the head meets the body. Help: 5.15.1 (Reading: Searching the array)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Am I in my own tail?". The task: before the snake moves, loop over the body and compare each segment with the cell the head is about to enter, and set a lost flag when they match. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic. Accept any names, helpers, arrow functions and ternaries. A line only in a comment or string does not count. Use short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name their own line when something is missing, never write corrected code.

rubric.title: The next cell is tested
rubric.description: The comparison is against the cell the head is about to move into, not the current one.

rubric.title: Every segment
rubric.description: A loop checks all body segments, not just the first.

rubric.title: The round ends
rubric.description: A flag stops the stepping and the game shows that it is over.
